title: Food Delivery
summary: A food delivery platform coordinates three parties who each move at their own pace: a customer who wants food fast, a restaurant that needs time to cook, and a courier who should arrive just as the food is ready. The order service runs a strict state machine and holds the payment, the dispatch engine matches orders to couriers by predicted arrival time rather than raw distance, and couriers stream GPS so everyone sees live progress. Most of the hard problems are timing problems: predicting prep and travel time well enough that food is neither cold nor waiting.

walkthrough.title: Quote a delivery time
walkthrough.text: When the customer opens the checkout, the order service asks the ETA service for a quote: predicted prep time at this restaurant right now plus predicted travel time. The app shows a range such as 30-40 min.

walkthrough.title: Place the order
walkthrough.text: The app sends POST /orders with an Idempotency-Key. The order service creates the order in state CREATED and places an authorization hold on the card; nothing is charged yet, so a cancelled order costs the customer nothing.

walkthrough.title: Restaurant confirms
walkthrough.text: The order is pushed to the restaurant's tablet or POS integration. Staff accept it and confirm a prep time (say 15 min), or reject it because an item is sold out. Unconfirmed orders escalate to a phone call after about 3 minutes.

walkthrough.title: Hand off to dispatch
walkthrough.text: An order.accepted event with the expected ready_at time goes to the dispatch engine. Dispatch deliberately waits so the courier arrives at ready_at, not immediately; an early courier is an idle courier.

walkthrough.title: Score couriers and batches
walkthrough.text: Every few seconds dispatch collects open orders and nearby couriers from the geospatial index, asks the ETA service for a travel-time matrix, and solves an assignment problem. Two orders from the same restaurant may be batched onto one courier if neither gets more than a few minutes later.

walkthrough.title: Offer to a courier
walkthrough.text: The chosen courier gets an offer with pay and route and roughly 30 seconds to accept. A decline or timeout sends the order back into the next matching round, and the courier app starts streaming GPS every 4 seconds.

walkthrough.title: Pickup and live tracking
walkthrough.text: The courier navigates with turn-by-turn routes, marks the order picked up, and each GPS ping updates the geospatial index and the customer's live map. Trip events (picked_up, arriving) flow to the notification service.

walkthrough.title: Deliver, notify, and capture
walkthrough.text: On delivered, the customer gets a push notification, the order moves to DELIVERED, and the order service captures the payment, including the final tip. Actual prep and travel times are logged to retrain the ETA models.

data.label: Customer App

input.name: Order status & ETA
input.type: JSON: { orderId, state: "PREPARING" | "PICKED_UP" | "DELIVERED", eta: { min, max } }

output.name: Place order
output.type: POST /v1/orders { restaurantId, items[], addressId, tip } + Idempotency-Key

responsibilities: Builds the cart, shows the quoted delivery window, and places the order with a client-generated idempotency key.
Renders live order state and the courier's position on a map during delivery.

failureModes.scenario: Customer taps 'Place order' twice on a slow network
failureModes.impact: Two identical orders and two card holds.
failureModes.mitigation: The idempotency key is generated once per checkout; the server returns the original order for a repeat.

failureModes.scenario: WebSocket drops while the customer watches the map
failureModes.impact: The courier icon freezes and the customer assumes the order is stuck.
failureModes.mitigation: Reconnect with backoff, fall back to polling every 15 s, and show 'last updated' time.

data.label: Order Service

output.name: To dispatch
output.type: Event: order.accepted { orderId, restaurantId, readyAt, dropoff: { lat, lng } }

responsibilities: Owns the order state machine: CREATED → CONFIRMED → PREPARING → PICKED_UP → DELIVERED (or CANCELLED), rejecting illegal transitions.
Deduplicates placement by idempotency key, places an authorization hold at checkout, and captures only on delivery.
Publishes every state change to Kafka for dispatch, notifications, and analytics.

failureModes.scenario: Payment provider times out, then the request is retried
failureModes.impact: The customer sees two holds, or is double-charged on capture.
failureModes.mitigation: Pass the order id as the provider's idempotency key; reconcile unknown authorizations before retrying.

failureModes.impact: The customer waits with a hold on their card and no food in progress.
failureModes.mitigation: Timer per state: auto-call the restaurant after ~3 min, auto-cancel and release the hold after ~10 min.

data.label: Restaurant Tablet & POS Integration

input.name: New order
input.type: JSON: { orderId, items[], notes, pickupBy } (push / POS webhook)

responsibilities: Alerts staff loudly until an order is accepted or rejected, and captures their prep-time estimate.
Marks items out of stock and pauses the store when the kitchen is overwhelmed.

failureModes.scenario: Tablet offline or muted during the dinner rush
failureModes.impact: Orders sit unconfirmed; food is late or never made.
failureModes.mitigation: Heartbeat monitoring, automated phone call fallback, and auto-pause the store after repeated misses.

failureModes.scenario: Staff accept with the default prep time regardless of load
failureModes.impact: Couriers arrive early and wait, or food sits and goes cold.
failureModes.mitigation: ETA service learns each store's real prep time and overrides the stated value when they disagree.

data.label: ETA Prediction Service

output.name: Prediction
output.type: JSON: { prepMin: 14, travelMin: { courierId: 9 }, p50: 28, p90: 37 }

responsibilities: Predicts prep time from the restaurant's live order queue, time of day, and history, and travel time from the routing matrix plus courier speed.
Returns ranges (p50 / p90) rather than one number, so the app can promise a window it will usually meet.
Retrains daily on actual prep and delivery times logged from completed orders.

failureModes.scenario: ETAs too optimistic at peak (Friday 7 pm, rain)
failureModes.impact: Missed promises, refunds, and couriers dispatched too early.
failureModes.mitigation: Features for live demand, weather, and kitchen backlog; monitor ETA error per city per hour.

failureModes.impact: Checkout and dispatch both lose their timing signal.
failureModes.mitigation: 20 ms budget with fallback to per-restaurant historical averages plus straight-line distance.

data.label: Dispatch & Assignment Engine

input.name: Ready orders
input.type: Event: order.accepted { orderId, readyAt, pickup, dropoff }

input.name: Courier locations
input.type: GPS ping: { courierId, lat, lng, heading, ts } every 4 s

output.name: Courier offer
output.type: Push: { offerId, orderIds[], payout, pickupAt, expiresIn: 30 }

responsibilities: Keeps courier positions in a geospatial index (H3 cells) and finds candidates near each pickup in milliseconds.
Every few seconds solves a batch assignment that minimises total lateness, matching by predicted arrival time rather than distance and batching compatible orders.
Re-assigns orders when an offer is declined, times out, or the courier stops moving.

failureModes.scenario: Two dispatch workers assign the same courier or order
failureModes.impact: Two couriers drive to one order, or one courier gets conflicting jobs.
failureModes.mitigation: Partition dispatch by city/zone and claim with a compare-and-set on the order's assignment version.

failureModes.scenario: Courier goes offline mid-delivery or GPS goes stale
failureModes.impact: The order looks in progress but nobody is moving; the customer's ETA is fiction.
failureModes.mitigation: Flag couriers with no ping for 60 s, call them, and re-dispatch if pickup has not happened.

failureModes.scenario: Dinner-time demand spike outruns courier supply
failureModes.impact: Unassigned orders pile up and delivery times stretch past an hour.
failureModes.mitigation: Surge pay to attract couriers, wider delivery-time quotes, and temporarily shrinking delivery radius.

data.label: Courier App

input.name: Offer
input.type: Push: { offerId, orderIds[], payout, pickupAt, expiresIn: 30 }

output.name: Location
output.type: GPS ping: { courierId, lat, lng, accuracyM, ts } every 4 s

responsibilities: Shows offers, streams GPS every few seconds while on a job, and buffers pings when the network drops.
Records pickup and drop-off events with photo or PIN proof of delivery.

failureModes.scenario: Noisy or spoofed GPS (tunnels, high-rises, fake-location apps)
failureModes.impact: Wrong ETAs, or fake deliveries marked complete.
failureModes.mitigation: Snap pings to roads, drop low-accuracy fixes, and require geofenced drop-off plus proof photo.

failureModes.scenario: Phone OS kills the background app
failureModes.impact: Location stops; dispatch thinks the courier vanished.
failureModes.mitigation: Foreground service with persistent notification; dispatch tolerates short gaps before re-assigning.

data.label: Maps & Routing Provider
responsibilities: Returns travel-time matrices for dispatch scoring and turn-by-turn routes for couriers, with live traffic.
Geocodes addresses and stores drop-off pins and entrance notes.

failureModes.scenario: Provider quota exhausted or latency spikes
failureModes.impact: Dispatch rounds slow down or stall.
failureModes.mitigation: Self-hosted OSRM for bulk matrices, cache travel times per H3 cell pair, paid API only for final routes.

failureModes.scenario: Bad geocode for a new building
failureModes.impact: Courier goes to the wrong entrance; delivery takes 10 extra minutes.
failureModes.mitigation: Let customers drag the pin; learn corrected drop-off points from past deliveries.

data.label: Notification Service

output.name: Customer alert
output.type: Push: "Your courier is 2 min away" + live-location channel

responsibilities: Turns order and trip events into push, SMS, and in-app messages, deduplicated per event id.
Fans live courier location to the customer's open tracking session.

failureModes.mitigation: Compare against the order's current state version and drop stale notifications.

failureModes.scenario: Push provider delays during a spike
failureModes.impact: Customers miss 'courier arriving' and the courier waits at the door.
failureModes.mitigation: SMS fallback for arrival alerts; courier app offers a one-tap masked call.
